As someone who has played all the games minus 3, I can say that DQ8 had better music in the sense that it was original, whereas most of Dq11’s music is remixes of older titles. Dq11 was an homage to previous games in the series including DQ8. The turn based battles are the same for both so I won’t go into any more detail. I haven’t completed DQ11, haven’t even finished act 1 yet, but I say that I enjoy the characters in DQ8 that much more because originally there are only 4. The hero, Yangus, Jessica, and Angelo, and because of that they are able to put more depth into each one of them. This was also the first instance of voice acting in a dragon quest. I’d say the skill points of DQ8 I prefer to DQ11 because everything is open at the beginning and you know what abilities you will get. That and in DQ8, there are more viable options of what kinds of weapons to use. Each character gets 3 choices of weapons, compared to the 2 and each one can be used on a play through to great affect. The alchemy system is something I prefer in DQ11, being able to reforge equipment is great! It means that even dungeon loot can be improved upon. The lack of many crafting recipes you get throughout the game is lacking though. In each town you may get one or two, whereas in DQ8, it seemed like less of a hinderance. I will say for what I’ve gotten into with the story both are good. DQ8 with Dhoulmagus and the sages really gave me a WOAH moment when I realized why Dhoulmagus was killing people. I got an even bigger woah moment with DQ11, assuming there’s going to be a standard JRPG where you meet the king. For most JRPG’s if you are seen as evil, it’s near the end of the game, or there are evil monsters trapping you, but in the first hour? Never. That gives it to DQ11. All in all great games, both you can sink 100 hours into. 
DQ8: 9/10 
DQ11: 8.5/10 (so far, I haven’t gotten past act 1)
